title: Proverbs Bible Quiz - Chapter 14
description: Ten questions on Proverbs 14: the wise woman who builds her house, the way that seems right, and the fear of Yahweh as a fountain of life.

questions.text: What does the foolish woman do, in contrast with the wise woman who builds her house?
questions.explanation: Every wise woman builds her house, but the foolish one tears it down with her own hands.

answers.text: She lets it fall into ruin
She tears it down with her own hands

questions.text: How does the saying go: "Where no oxen are, the crib is clean, but..."?
questions.explanation: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean, but much increase is by the strength of the ox.

answers.text: the field lies fallow and bears nothing
much increase is by the strength of the ox
the farmer labors for his bread in vain
the barn stands empty at the harvest

questions.text: What does the heart know, which it will not share with a stranger?
questions.explanation: The heart knows its own bitterness and joy; he will not share these with a stranger.

questions.text: Where does the way which seems right to a man lead in the end?
questions.explanation: There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.

questions.text: What does a simple man do, in contrast with the prudent man?
questions.explanation: A simple man believes everything, but the prudent man carefully considers his ways.

questions.text: What does this chapter say about the poor person and the rich person among their neighbors and friends?
questions.explanation: The poor person is shunned even by his own neighbor, but the rich person has many friends.

answers.text: The poor person is honored, but the rich person is envied
Both are tested by their friends
The poor person has true friends, but the rich person has flatterers
The poor person is shunned even by his own neighbor, but the rich person has many friends

questions.text: What is in all hard work, in contrast with the talk of the lips?
questions.explanation: In all hard work there is profit, but the talk of the lips leads only to poverty.

questions.text: What does he who is slow to anger have, in contrast with a quick temper?
questions.explanation: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.

questions.text: What does he who oppresses the poor show, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: He who oppresses the poor shows contempt for his Maker, but he who is kind to the needy honors him.

questions.text: How does the saying go: "Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin..."?
questions.explanation: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.

answers.text: is a disgrace to any people
